text: Lesson 30 closed Teresa Marsh's incident with a filed, owned after-action report, but closing a report doesn't close an attacker's broader campaign. This lesson runs Chapter 7's hypothesis-driven hunting loop for real, turning this incident's own root cause into a specific question — and finding a second compromised account the original alert never touched at all.

The hunt team frames a precise hypothesis, not a vague one: did the attacker use a different persistence technique, from the same credential-theft wave, against a second identity whose sign-in geography would look ordinary and never trip impossible travel? That second half matters — repeating Teresa's exact indicators would miss an attacker who varied the pattern on purpose.

The hunt pivots to a technique Sentinel has no rule for at all: inbox forwarding rules, MITRE ATT&CK T1114.003. A query against OfficeActivity for New-InboxRule and Set-Mailbox operations, filtered to rules forwarding outside the tenant's own domain, is what the investigate step of Chapter 7's loop actually looks like in practice.

The query returns one account the SOC had never flagged: Daniel Oyelaran, a Compliance Operations Analyst, with a rule created nine days before Teresa's incident, silently forwarding any email containing "wire" or "transfer" to an external Gmail address — created from a residential IP in his own normal metro area.

A hunt that stays a one-time manual query never catches the next version of this. The team schedules the same query as a new Sentinel analytics rule, run hourly, entity-mapped to the mailbox owner's account, tagged to T1114.003 — so the next forwarding rule aimed at client financial mail raises an incident on its own.

Detection, scoping, evidence-safe containment, eradication, recovery, a real after-action report, and a hunt that closed a gap the SIEM never covered — every chapter of this course, run on one real incident. The final lesson reviews all eight chapters, the six courses underneath them, and what this stage now makes you ready for.
